title: Chocolate Fudge Cupcakes with Milk Chocolate Swirl Frosting
description: These cupcakes are for anyone who wants a real chocolate hit, not a light cocoa suggestion. The batter uses melted chocolate plus cocoa powder, so the crumb bakes moist and fudgy, not dry and crumbly.
shortDescription: Deep cocoa fudge cupcakes take 25 minutes to prep and 18 minutes to bake, topped with tall milk chocolate buttercream swirls.

metaDescription: Bake moist chocolate fudge cupcakes with milk chocolate swirl frosting. Easy recipe, ready in 43 minutes. Get the full step-by-step plan now.
ingredients: 3 oz semisweet chocolate, melted and cooled
8 oz milk chocolate, melted and cooled (for frosting)
instructions: Heat oven to 350°F. Line a 12 cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk flour, cocoa powder, both sugars, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, mix buttermilk, hot coffee, oil, egg, and vanilla.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Whisk until smooth.
Stir in the melted semisweet chocolate until the batter looks glossy and even.
Divide batter among liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool cupcakes in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a wire rack to cool fully.
Beat softened butter on medium speed until pale and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Add melted milk chocolate and beat until combined.
Add powdered sugar in two batches, mixing on low, then add cream and salt. Beat on high 1 minute until light.
Pipe frosting high in a swirl on each cooled cupcake using a large star tip.
tips: Use hot coffee instead of water. It sharpens the cocoa flavor without tasting like coffee.
Let melted chocolate cool to room temperature before adding it to batter or butter, so it does not melt the butter or cook the egg.
Weigh your flour or spoon it into the measuring cup and level it. Packed flour makes dense cupcakes.
Chill piped cupcakes 10 minutes before serving so the swirl holds its shape in a warm kitchen.
conclusion: These cupcakes give you real fudge flavor in the cake and a milk chocolate swirl that piles up tall. Bake a batch when you want chocolate that actually tastes like chocolate.

faq.question: Why do these cupcakes use coffee in the batter?
faq.answer: Hot coffee deepens the cocoa flavor without making the cupcakes taste like coffee. Hot water works too, but the chocolate flavor is less bold.

faq.question: Can I use dark chocolate instead of milk chocolate in the frosting?
faq.answer: Yes, swap in the same amount of dark chocolate for a less sweet frosting. Keep the powdered sugar the same so the texture still pipes well.

faq.question: Why did my frosting turn grainy or split?
faq.answer: This happens when the melted chocolate is still warm when added to butter. Let it cool fully to room temperature first, then mix on medium speed, not high.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to 2 days ahead and store them unfrosted in an airtight container at room temperature. Frost the same day you plan to serve them for the best swirl.
